newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen Industrie sees higher profit.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen Industrie sees higher profit.

text.p: Thyssen Industrie AG, the capital goods division of German steel and engineering group Thyssen AG, said on Monday profit on ordinary activities in the 1996/97 business year would rise to over 250 million marks ($154.1 million).

Chairman Eckhard Rohkamm told a news conference that profit on ordinaries would rise further to more than 350 million marks in the 1997/98 business year on the condition that the German economy continues to recover.
For the business year that ended on September 30, 1996, Thyssen Industrie reported that group net profit fell to 65 million marks from 104 million marks the year before.
Group sales rose to 9.147 billion marks from 8.497 billion marks and profit on ordinary activities rose to 239 million from 194 million.

Incoming orders fell to 9.7 billion marks from 10.1 billion and cash flow was lower at 392 million marks from 463 million marks. The company will pay a dividend of 4.80 marks, down from six marks the year before.
The workforce remained fairly steady, with 42,217 employees on average for the year compared to 42,511 the year before.
